conclusion: No full-YOLO speedup from these adapted register or subgroup-matrix routes on this adapter. Keep experimental adapters opt-in; default runtime and model artifacts unchanged.
scope: Direct adaptations of the published Conv register and subgroup-matrix templates, not generic kernels inspired by HF.
1x1 direct register GEMM, 3x3 implicit gathering, 64/32-row register tiles, K16/32, published carried-gather mode 1.

Experimental matrix: aligned 1x1 plus implicit 3x3 with K tails, FP32 accumulation and 32-lane subgroups; request up to 32KiB workgroup storage when adapter permits. Both baseline and HF variants share the same device/limits.
The complete HF loader/selection heuristics, split-K, explicit im2col, other operators and graph fusion are not implemented or assessed.

15 raw convolution shapes, both precisions, 8 warmups and 51 rotated samples, dispatches recorded once. GPU timestamps for repeated raw kernels; submit+sync wall time for unchanged full YOLO graph. No camera/pre/post/presentation.
Two independent runs; absolute times vary with device/browser state. Use paired within-run ratios. Findings are for this Apple/Metal adapter and Chrome, not a cross-hardware ranking.
numerics: All model variants pass the existing project PyTorch fixture tolerances: f32 abs <=0.01 everywhere; f16 abs <=0.5 for at least 95% of output elements. These are existing tolerances, not bitwise equivalence.
HF preserves FP32 accumulation even for FP16 storage. Baseline uses FP16 accumulation. FP16 comparisons include an accuracy/performance tradeoff.

22 Node CPU-oracle cases cover register routes, tails, batches, stride, dilation and optional bias. Browser CPU oracles independently cover both matrix routes, batch2, partial tiles and absent bias; poisoned outputs detect missing writes.
Raw HF outputs match the rounded F32 reference on deliberately dyadic inputs. This exactness is specific to these bounded diagnostic inputs, not a general exact-output claim.

reproduce.shaderGeneration: Install Jinja2 in a separate Python environment, then run utils/benchmark/adapt-hf-conv.py and utils/benchmark/adapt-hf-matrix.py. Generated shaders are committed; normal tests and benchmarks require no Python/Jinja2.
